name: Erik Schmidt

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm a field researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We don't sell anything or campaign for a side, and this is confidential. What does an ordinary working day look like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Erik Schmidt, twenty-seven, and I lead the small-business team at North Ledger. I have a master's and a chartered accountancy qualification, and the pay is about usual for this job. I start with shop accounts, review tax returns, then phone owners when a number needs a story. The last hour is usually a queue of questions from my team.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: Which part do you like, and what wears you out?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I like the moment a shop owner understands where the cash went. The filing rush is exhausting, and I dislike correcting the same missing receipt twice. I use AI now and then when another accountant has tested a tool, but I still check the file myself. Nia and I have four months of expenses saved, no children, and some other firms close enough to commute to.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A quieter future would suit our office fine. The software I try now and then formats a covering letter, but it cannot tell a shop owner why their cash drawer is short.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the team the new tools are useful for small jobs, provided we check the numbers. I'd tell clients our fees still pay for a person who owns the answer, not just a printed return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be relieved, mostly. I'm twenty-seven, lead the small-business team at North Ledger, and earn the usual rate for a chartered accountant. My partner Nia and I have four months of expenses saved, and there are some other firms nearby if I needed a move.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep reviewing the team's returns and use the letter tool only where another accountant has already tested it. I'd keep the automatic transfer of two hundred a month into savings. In the first year of this plateau, I would ask the partners for one extra trainee, because the queue of small shops is growing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about my own bills and job, although deadlines are still tiring. A quiet change would let me improve the old process rather than redesign my life.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can you give me a moment that still needs you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last spring the bakery owner brought a tin of mixed receipts in on filing day. We found an old supplier invoice behind the till slip, which was the missing expense. The machine could sort the slips, but somebody had to ask about the oven repair.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why ask for another trainee?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd show the partners our waiting list and the hours the team spends correcting late records. I wouldn't hire on a promise from a tool supplier. If the shop work stays as it is, a trainee would pay for their place in a few months.

say: I would present **AI** as a small aid for letters and sorting.
I would tell clients a **person** remains answerable for their returns.
think: My **pay and cushion** leave me secure in this picture.
Some **nearby firms** give me room if North Ledger changes.
do: Keep reviewing **shop returns** and tested letter drafts.
Ask partners for a **trainee** if the shop queue holds.
feel: I feel **calm** about my job and bills.
S0.quote: The machine could sort the slips, but somebody had to ask about the oven repair.
fieldNote: His **four-month cushion** and local alternatives support a calm view of a modest change.
The **bakery example** explains why he still expects demand for client questions and review.

steps.text: Keep reviewing small-shop tax returns and tested letter drafts
Transfer two hundred monthly into household savings

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Bank sorting is the first crack, and this picture widens it. If the tool also checks, books and writes, we might finish the same queue with fewer people.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At work I'd say we should measure errors as well as hours saved. I'd tell friends there is no point promising everyone a new job until someone shows where those jobs are.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The partners might keep me to handle owners and sign returns, but freeze a junior vacancy. That would make me responsible for more files and fewer pairs of eyes. My salary is typical, yet the team could shrink and my own hours could follow.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd take twenty recent shop returns and compare the tool's checks with our signed work this quarter. If the results hold, I'd learn its review panel with my team. I'd ask the partners to replace any departing junior for one filing season before using the saved hours as a headcount target.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the team, with some control over the test. Four months of savings gives me time, but it doesn't protect colleagues from a vacancy freeze.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which person on your team is most exposed?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Petra, my junior colleague, is finishing her qualification and has a rented flat. I'd put her on the comparison exercise so she can show where a tax code was wrong. My junior colleague should be measured by errors caught, not just entries keyed per hour.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What evidence would you bring to the partners?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask for the error list, client complaints and actual filing time on one page. If the partners say the new tool saves a post, I want them to show which duties vanish and who takes responsibility for mistakes. I'd then take those figures to the staff meeting. I'd ask colleagues at the staff meeting to back a rule on replacing junior vacancies.

say: I would demand **error measures** beside saved hours before the partners cut any junior vacancy.
I would ask where promised **new jobs** actually are.
think: A frozen **junior vacancy** could increase my load and leave Petra without a clear route.
My own **hours** may shrink if the team contracts.
do: Compare **twenty returns** with the tool this quarter.
Learn its **review panel** with the team if tests hold.
Ask partners to **replace juniors** through one filing season.
feel: I feel **anxious** about the team and my hours.
S1.quote: My junior colleague should be measured by errors caught, not just entries keyed per hour.
fieldNote: A **twenty-return test** fits his preference for tools proven on real files.
The **junior vacancy** worry reaches his workload and possibly his own hours in the next filing season.

steps.text: Compare twenty returns and learn AI review panel if checks hold
Ask colleagues to back junior vacancy replacement rule at staff meeting

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2028 leaves almost no time for a practice like ours. We buy software after two filing seasons of watching other firms, and this would arrive before that habit helped.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say publicly that staff need notice and temporary income if firms cut fast. I'd ask North Ledger's partners for a written plan this winter, including who carries liability when a system signs off in effect.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my return-preparation job to disappear soon after full AGI in 2028. It's mostly thinking at a screen, so the robots arriving around 2031 do not give me three more years. Four months of savings and a few local firms help, but those firms could face the same shock.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd move the two hundred monthly savings transfer to four hundred by cancelling weekend trips with Nia. This winter I'd apply for the council's open finance controller post if the salary covers our rent. In the first year after 2028, if North Ledger cuts me, I'd use the savings to pay rent while I apply outside accounting. If the layoff comes, I'd apply for temporary income support while I search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, because I can see the whole market changing together. Four months of savings buys me time, but I would still lose sleep over finding another accounting wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does your partner enter the decision?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nia works at a library, so there is a second wage, but her salary alone won't cover our rent. I'd tell her about the applications before I sent them, not after an offer appeared. We would freeze the holiday plan together.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What gets cut and which vacancy matters?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Rent and groceries stay on the account; travel goes first. I'd check the controller vacancy is funded and pays enough before applying. If it has already closed, I'd contact the council recruiter about the next opening rather than quit my current post.

say: I would request **notice and income support** for displaced staff.
I would ask partners for a **written liability plan** this winter.
think: My **screen-based post** may end soon after 2028.
Four months of **savings** may not outlast a sector-wide shock.
do: Raise savings to **four hundred monthly** by cancelling trips.
Apply for a **funded council post** if salary covers rent.
Apply for **income support** after a layoff while our cushion pays rent and I search beyond accounting.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about a shared market shock.
S2.quote: Four months of savings buys me time, but I would still lose sleep over finding another accounting wage.
fieldNote: His **screen work** is exposed at AGI in 2028 rather than the later robot date.
A **second wage** and four months saved soften immediate harm, but neither secures rent if firms cut together.

steps.text: Cancel weekend trips and save four hundred monthly
Apply for funded council controller post if pay covers rent
Apply for income support after a 2028 layoff while seeking work

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years is enough to collect evidence, which matters more to me than a bold prediction. I'd still expect return preparation to change sharply when full AGI arrives in 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the partners to publish what they expect to automate and to pay for staff learning. To friends I'd say a slower date helps only if we begin while the jobs still exist.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might move into finance control for a hospital or council, where rules and accountability make the transition slower. I wouldn't call it safe forever, because the thinking work is still exposed. But five years gives me time to test whether I like the work and save more than four months.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'd enrol in the evening public-finance course if North Ledger pays the five-hundred fee. I'd take two paid afternoons observing the council's finance office if my manager approves release. I'd keep saving two hundred monthly, and in the first year after AGI in 2031 I'd apply for a funded controller vacancy if my tax role ends and the salary covers rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, though I can name a sequence of steps. The extra three years compared with 2028 make a course and a real placement possible.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who pays for the course and placement time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five hundred is affordable from savings, but I won't drain the emergency pot for a course the firm needs. I'd put the funding request in writing and use free council accounts workshops if it is refused. The paid release matters too, because I cannot learn the role from a brochure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the placement useful?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the council manager to let me follow a year-end close and talk through one disputed payment. If I can't get that access, I'd judge the course on its own and keep my applications open. I need evidence that council finance work differs from preparing tax returns before I change jobs.

say: I would ask the firm to publish **automation plans**.
I would argue for **paid learning** before posts disappear.
think: A **controller role** may offer a transition, not permanent safety.
Five years could grow my **cash cushion** beyond four months.
do: Study **public finance** through a funded course or free workshops; observe council cases only on approved paid release.
Keep saving **two hundred monthly** from my pay.
Apply for a **funded controller vacancy** after 2031 if tax work ends and pay covers rent.
feel: I feel **anxious**, though I have time to test a route.
S3.quote: I need evidence that council finance work differs from preparing tax returns before I change jobs.
fieldNote: Firm-paid **course fees** and release time turn a possible career shift into actual learning.
He sees a **funded controller post** as a conditional landing after 2031, not a permanent refuge.

steps.text: Take funded public-finance course or free council workshops if course fee refused
Observe council finance on paid afternoons if manager approves
Apply for funded controller vacancy after 2031 if pay covers rent
Keep saving two hundred monthly from salary

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years lets me plan without pretending the endpoint changes. I'd be thirty-seven, and the tax-return desk may be smaller or gone by 2036.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say we should use the time to reduce hours gradually as routine returns get faster. I'd also ask clients to keep a named person accountable for their records, because a cheap answer can still be wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could build toward teaching accounting or helping small businesses keep good records before an audit. Neither is untouched by thinking AI, but those roles let me use what I know while I have time. My tax work is exposed in 2036; robots in 2039 do not extend the deadline.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'd offer one short workshop for shop owners through the business centre, if it has a paid place. I'd keep the two-hundred monthly savings transfer and ask the college about its part-time teaching qualification next spring. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, if my return role ends, I'd apply for a funded teaching vacancy only if its hours and salary cover our rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy but fairly steady. A decade lets me try a class before telling Nia I am changing careers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes teaching more than a vague idea?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I once spent forty minutes showing a mechanic how to separate parts from labour on an invoice. He sent the next month's records in order, which saved both of us time. That felt closer to teaching than to filing a return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask before leaving North Ledger?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the business centre to pay for the first workshop, even if it is only a small fee. Then I'd ask the college about funded openings and the qualification they require. I will not resign for a course catalogue.

say: I would seek **gradual hour cuts** as returns speed up.
I would keep a **named accountant** answerable to clients.
think: My **tax desk** still contracts when AGI reaches it in 2036.
A decade lets me test **teaching** with actual shop owners.
do: Run one **paid workshop** if the business centre offers a place.
Apply after 2036 for **funded teaching work** if its hours and pay cover rent.
feel: I feel **uneasy**, but time gives me room to test.
S4.quote: I will not resign for a course catalogue.
fieldNote: A **paid workshop** is his practical test of a possible teaching route.
The **2036 application** depends on a funded vacancy with enough hours and pay to cover rent.

steps.text: Run paid bookkeeping workshop if business centre offers a place
Save two hundred monthly in household account
Apply for funded teaching vacancy after 2036 if hours and pay cover rent

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my desk work is exposed at once and other firms may cut at the same time. A short income bridge, notice from the partners and funded training linked to actual vacancies would help. Four months of savings will not fix a whole market. I'd need to know who is hiring, not merely what course is offered.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You didn't ask who checks a return when a system does nearly all of it. The client will still get a tax bill with a name on top. I want the firm to say plainly who is accountable before it celebrates faster filing.

headlineQuote: The client will still get a tax bill with a name on top.
portrait: At **twenty-seven**, Erik leads small-business accounts and tax returns at North Ledger.
His **master’s** and chartered qualification earn typical pay, and his household has four months saved.
He tries **AI occasionally** after peers test it, and he checks figures himself.
Some **nearby firms** give him options, though full AGI could hit them together.
He favours **measured pilots**, paid learning and funded vacancies over promises of safe new careers.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his screen-based work while nearby firms face the same shock.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **notice**, temporary income and funded training connected to real vacancies.
